subject: computer-science
title: Recursion: Base Cases and Stacks
welcome_lead: A function calling itself — done safely.
meta_desc: A-Level CS: base case, recursive case and the call stack.
final_note: Every recursion must shrink toward a base case.

concepts.def: The case where the function calls itself on a smaller input.
The stack of active function calls during execution.
Error when the call stack runs out of space.
Two or more functions that call each other in a cycle.

walkthroughs.body_html: Every recursive function needs a base case (when to stop) and a recursive case (smaller subproblem). Without a reachable base case, recursion runs forever and overflows the stack.
Each call pushes a stack frame with local variables and return address. Too many calls (deep recursion) cause a stack overflow. Languages with tail-call optimisation can reuse frames.
Direct recursion: f calls f. Indirect: f calls g, which calls f. Both must reach a base case along every path.
